title: Pyrelisk and the Splitting Embers
story: In the ash pits below Mount Grindle, Pyrelisk begins as a single ember-imp, but every time a sword clangs against stone it splits into three. Mr 6 taps his blade on the rock once just to test the legend — and then, wisely, stops and starts counting instead.
question: Starting with 1 ember-imp, if the number triples with each of 5 clangs, how many ember-imps would there be after the 5th clang?
hint: Start at 1 and triple it once for each clang: 1, 3, 9... keep going until you've done all five clangs.
victory: Mr 6 sheathed his sword, whispered the number 243 aloud, and Pyrelisk — who only grew when struck — sputtered out from sheer boredom into one sleepy, harmless spark.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight holding his sword deliberately still while tiny grinning ember-imps multiply across a smoky volcanic ash pit, orange firelight glowing on his helmet.
praise: Seeing that the imps triple each time was the key idea — the step to watch is repeating the tripling a full five times instead of stopping early.
